stories.title: Oil edges up on Houthi strikes and Hormuz mines, but heads for a third weekly loss
stories.lead: Brent rose 0.6% to $92.57 on Friday morning and December WTI 0.5% to $83.63, yet Brent is on track for about -3.5% on the week and December WTI for nearly -6%.
stories.body: Houthi missiles targeted Riyadh and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. On Thursday Brent settled at $92.71 (+0.8%) after a New York Times report that Washington was weighing new strikes on Iran; Trump later said he would decide after the start of 2027. Against that, the IEA expects a supply surplus, US crude stocks rose for a second week and Kpler data show Hormuz flows recovering. The December WTI contract expires today.
stories.why: Geopolitical risk premium and a heavy physical market are cancelling out ahead of the OPEC+ ministerial meeting on 29 November.

stories.title: Wall Street drops 2% and Asia heads for its worst week since 2020 as the Anthropic debut fails to lift AI
stories.lead: The S&P 500 fell about 2% to a seven-month low on Thursday, the Nasdaq 2.3% and the Dow 2.2%, with the VIX at 28.4; on Friday Taiwan fell 6.6%, the Kospi 5.2% and the Nikkei 4.8%.
stories.body: All eleven S&P 500 sectors fell. Anthropic closed its first session at $97.17, 17% above its $83 IPO price, then slipped 6.3% after hours. Nvidia lost 3.3% and AMD 7.7%; in Asia SoftBank fell 15% and the Hang Seng entered a bear market. MSCI Asia ex-Japan is set for about -8.6% on the week, its worst since early 2020.
stories.why: Risk aversion drives margin calls and a stronger dollar, which spill into gold, copper and the wider commodity complex.

stories.title: Gold hits a 14-month low and copper a seven-month low
stories.lead: Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,554 after touching $3,513.54, its lowest since September 2025, and is heading for about -9% on the week; LME copper dropped 2.4% to $12,190.68 a tonne.
stories.body: A dollar near a 19-month high and a 97.3% probability of a 25bp Fed hike in December (CME FedWatch) weigh on bullion, while investors sell gold to meet margin calls as AI stocks slump. Platinum fell 2.2% to $1,320.60 and US copper 1.3% to $5.52 a pound.
stories.why: Gold behaving as a source of cash in a selloff, rather than a haven, is a classic feature of margin-driven markets.

stories.title: Dollar at a 19-month high while the US 10-year yield falls to 5.016%
stories.lead: The dollar index held near 103.9, up eight sessions in a row, while the US 10-year yield slipped to a one-week low of 5.016%, down about 10bp on the week.
stories.body: Safe-haven demand and hawkish Fed signals support the dollar: EUR/USD is at $1.0972 and USD/JPY at 159.50. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee warned that AI-driven demand could overheat the economy. In Japan, core inflation came in at 2.2% in October against 2.3% expected, with a Bank of Japan hike to 1.5% still expected on 18 December.
stories.why: A strong dollar makes dollar-priced commodities more expensive for most buyers and weighs on metals and grains.

stories.title: TSMC tightens AI chip curbs on China after new US rules; chip stocks slide
stories.lead: According to Reuters, TSMC is tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers after new US rules closed a manufacturing loophole; its shares fell about 5% to a seven-month low.
stories.body: Advantest dropped 10.5% and Samsung and SK Hynix lost 6 to 7%. It is the second export-control blow to the sector this week, after a short seller accused AMD of supplying a blacklisted Chinese server maker.
stories.why: Export controls now shape demand for the chips that drive data-centre power and copper consumption.

stories.title: Oil holds near $92 as Trump weighs new Iran strikes, Russian refining is hit and US stocks build
stories.lead: Brent was steady at $92.18 (+0.25%) and WTI at $82.33 early on Thursday, after WTI fell 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest since 26 August on a 3.4 million barrel US crude build.
stories.body: The New York Times reports that President Trump is considering another round of extensive strikes on Iran under Israeli pressure, with no decision taken. The Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh on Thursday, Iran says three tankers were disabled by mines east of Hormuz, and Reuters industry sources say Ukrainian drones have cut Russian refinery crude runs by 45% since late October. Against that, Hormuz flows are back near pre-war levels and the IEA sees a surplus; Dutch TTF gas rebounded 2.4% to 82.80 euros per MWh.
stories.why: The market is pricing physical oversupply while escalation risk and a Russian product shortfall remain, so any decision on Iran strikes could reprice crude and diesel quickly.

stories.title: Fed minutes: nearly all officials see more hikes, a couple open to more than 25 bp in December
stories.lead: Minutes of the 27-28 October meeting, held at 3.75%-4.00%, show almost all participants expect further increases, and a couple say a move larger than 25 basis points could be considered on 9 December if inflation disappoints.
stories.body: Governor Waller argues for 50 bp or a clear signal of more hikes in 2027, while Williams, Hammack and Logan prefer a gradual path. CME FedWatch prices about 90-95% odds of 25 bp and about 5% of 50 bp. The US 10-year yield is near 5.07% and the dollar index near 103.8, a 19-month high; the minutes also flag risks from rising AI-related debt.
stories.why: A stronger dollar and higher real rates are the common driver behind this week's slide in gold, copper and grains.

stories.title: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in a record IPO as Taiwan's AI stocks slump 4.6%
stories.lead: Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83, above its $70-78 range, raising about $81.3 billion at a valuation near $1.5 trillion; it starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday.
stories.body: A further $26 billion private placement includes Nvidia and AMD, and Nasdaq 100 futures rose as much as 2%. Asia sold AI stocks anyway: Taiwan's index fell 4.6% to 38,347.67 (-14.9% this month), the Hang Seng lost 1.9%, and Nvidia closed 2.9% lower on Wednesday, 36% below its 6 October record. Foreign investors have sold more than NT$180 billion of Taiwanese shares in three sessions.
stories.why: AI demand drives copper, power and semiconductor supply chains, so a split between record funding and falling chip stocks matters well beyond equities.

stories.title: Gold rebounds from its lowest close since September 2025; copper steadies after a 6% drop
stories.lead: Spot gold rose 0.8% to $3,754.85 early on Thursday after a 3.2% fall on Wednesday; silver gained 1.4% to $45.72.
stories.body: Bargain hunters returned on central-bank buying, and ANZ calls the market oversold. Gold has lost about 30% since the US-Iran war began in late February, as costly energy lifted inflation and pushed central banks to tighten. COMEX copper was near $5.68 per pound (+0.3%) and LME copper near $12,533 per tonne (-0.3%) after Wednesday's slump.
stories.why: Gold falling during a war shows that real rates, not geopolitics, are setting the price for now.

stories.title: Corn hits a four-and-a-half-month low and Chicago wheat its lowest since January
stories.lead: On 18 November CBOT December corn fell 2.5% to $4.355 per bushel, its lowest since 30 June, and December wheat lost 25 cents to $5.7025.
stories.body: A stronger dollar ahead of a December Fed hike makes US grain less competitive, and weaker crude weighs on corn through ethanol, with output at 1.126 million barrels per day. Wheat gave back the premium from the Crimea bridge strike as traders looked to a US-China-Russia summit on Ukraine.
stories.why: Grain prices are being set by the dollar and energy as much as by crops, a link that matters for every export origin.

stories.title: Oil slips as US stocks swell, while attacks continue around Hormuz and the Saudi bypass pipeline
stories.lead: Brent fell 0.7% to $92.53 and WTI 1.4% to $84.77 early on Wednesday after the API reported US crude stocks up 5.28 million barrels and gasoline up 5.12 million barrels.
stories.body: Crude is building on the US Gulf Coast, which closes the WTI export arbitrage to Asia and northwest Europe and pushed the Brent-WTI spread to a two-week high. Risk has not gone away: Iranian drones targeted a US radar in Bahrain and the US struck a missile site on Qeshm island on Tuesday, an LPG tanker was hit near Hormuz on Monday, and the Houthis said they launched five drones at two pumping stations of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, with no damage confirmed. LSEG analysts see no normalisation of Hormuz flows under current conditions.
stories.why: The paper market is pricing an oversupplied US physical market while the main route around Hormuz is being targeted, an asymmetry that official EIA stock data later today will test.

stories.title: Nvidia beats with $115.8bn revenue and a $130bn outlook, but the stock barely moves
stories.lead: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.84bn, up 103% and above the $108.85bn expected, with data centre sales of $107.6bn, and guided to $130bn plus or minus 3% against about $125bn expected.
stories.body: The outlook excludes any data centre compute sales to China: Nvidia will stop shipping licensed Hopper products there, worth $2.4bn last quarter. Shares rose as much as 5% after hours before fading to about +0.7%, as the board ruled out the return of Jensen Huang and the Wall Street Journal reported an SEC probe into its disclosures. Before the release the S&P 500 closed 1.0% lower at 7,340.77, its lowest close since July 29, with the VIX at 25.46.
stories.why: AI demand is confirmed by the numbers, the main driver of copper and power demand from data centres, but investors no longer pay for growth alone; Anthropic's IPO pricing today tests the same appetite.

stories.title: Gold breaks below $3,800 and copper drops 2.9% as Fed officials talk up more hikes
stories.lead: Spot gold fell 1.5% to $3,790 and copper about 2.9% to $5.82 a pound early on Wednesday, with the dollar index at 103.65.
stories.body: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said several more rate increases are likely before spring and New York Fed President John Williams said there is more work to do on inflation. Markets price quarter-point hikes in December and January and another by April, and ANZ does not rule out 50 basis points next month. Copper is down about 11% in a month, with LME stocks near 320,000 tonnes against 205,000 in August; Fed minutes are due later today.
stories.why: Rising real rates weigh on gold, while a firm dollar and doubts over AI spending weigh on copper: two different mechanisms behind the same sell-off.

stories.title: European gas holds near EUR 84 with storage far below normal
stories.lead: Dutch TTF traded at EUR 84.11/MWh, down 1.5%, after holding above EUR 85 in the previous session; EU storage is about 70% full against a five-year average of 89%.
stories.body: Ship attacks around Hormuz threaten LNG cargoes from the Gulf and Qatari supply remains curtailed. German storage was below 58% on a November 17 reading, and colder weather in the forecast could speed up withdrawals.
stories.why: A 19-point storage gap before winter keeps European gas tight even as crude eases.

stories.title: Euronext wheat near a four-week high after the Crimea bridge strike
stories.lead: December wheat in Paris closed 0.2% higher at EUR 235.75 a tonne on Tuesday after touching EUR 238.75, and Chicago wheat gained about 2% from a four-month low.
stories.body: Ukraine's partial destruction of the Kerch bridge cut hopes of de-escalation after peace talks resumed. Gains were capped by the euro, which steadied after a 19-month low against the dollar, cheap Argentine wheat and Turkey's sale of 400,000 tonnes of milling wheat for export.
stories.why: The Black Sea remains the main risk premium in world wheat prices.

stories.title: European diesel margins fall as India taxes fuel exports
stories.lead: Northwest European diesel margins fell more than 5% on Monday: ICE low-sulphur gasoil traded $66.69 a barrel above Brent, down $3.64 on the session. India raised its export duty on diesel from 11.50 to 14 rupees a litre.
stories.body: Lower crude futures drove the drop in the crack. On the same day a Ukrainian strike damaged processing units at Russia's Ilsky refinery in the Krasnodar region, and India also raised its jet fuel export duty from 11 to 12.50 rupees a litre while leaving gasoline at zero, against wholesale inflation of 12.3% in October.
stories.why: Fewer Indian diesel cargoes heading west would support European cracks over time, even as falling crude pulls them down today.

stories.title: Wall Street falls a third day as chip stocks slump before Nvidia results
stories.lead: On Monday the S&P 500 fell 1.9% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq Composite 2.5% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index 5.3%; the VIX jumped 18.7% to 22.91. Nvidia lost 4.1% and is down nearly 24% in November.
stories.body: Nvidia's board is not considering a return of Jensen Huang, people familiar told Reuters, despite a petition with more than 180,000 signatures and support from President Trump; the company has lost about $800 billion in market value since the affair broke. It reports fiscal third-quarter results after the US close on Tuesday, with revenue of about $109 billion expected (LSEG).
stories.why: Chip makers drive demand for copper, power and specialty metals: a weak AI outlook would hit those trades too.

stories.title: US curbs Chinese access to AI chips through overseas data centres
stories.lead: A new Commerce Department rule requires export licences for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Taiwan's index closed 2.18% lower on Tuesday, Samsung fell 3.3% and TSMC 2.0%, while China's SMIC jumped 8.7%.
stories.body: Overseas data centres that rent significant computing power to companies based in China now need a licence, with 90 days for existing operators to comply, and the rule covers remote cloud access, not just physical shipments. Chinese AI groups fell (Baidu -6.8%, Alibaba -4.9%) while domestic chipmakers rallied on hopes of more local demand.
stories.why: Export controls now target services as well as goods, reshaping where data centres, and the power and copper they need, get built in Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Brent slips below $92 as US strategic reserve falls to a 1982 low
stories.lead: Brent traded around $91.5 on Tuesday morning, down about 1%, after falling 2.7% on Monday. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve stocks fell to 276.4 million barrels, the lowest since August 1982.
stories.body: Traders focus on the IEA's call for a fourth-quarter surplus as Gulf exports recover, and on Vice President Vance saying Washington wants to avoid a prolonged conflict with Iran. OPEC reviewed members' maximum production capacity on Monday ahead of the November 29 OPEC+ meeting on 2027 quotas, and Oman and Iran discussed shipping safety in Hormuz. European gas rose about 1.9% to near EUR 86/MWh, with EU storage below 71%.
stories.why: A depleted US reserve leaves less cushion against a new supply shock just as the market prices only the surplus.

stories.title: Gold rebounds from a 14-month low, copper at its lowest since June
stories.lead: Spot gold rose 0.7% to $3,881.59 an ounce on Tuesday, silver 1.6% to $47.75 and platinum 1.9%. Copper traded near $5.96 a pound, down 8.8% over a month.
stories.body: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack backed gradual rate increases, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no rate guidance on Monday; the minutes of the October meeting are due Wednesday. Copper is weighed down by the AI stock selloff, a firmer dollar and LME stocks of about 320,000 tonnes, up from 205,000 tonnes in August.
stories.why: Copper now trades as an AI infrastructure proxy, so Nvidia's results may move it as much as Chinese data.

stories.title: Iran claims mine strikes on three tankers in Hormuz, oil shrugs
stories.lead: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. Brent was at $95.37 (-0.49%) and WTI at $88.33 on Monday morning, after settling at $95.84 on Friday.
stories.body: The Guards said the unnamed tankers were using a prohibited route; Reuters could not verify the claim. On Sunday the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh and three drones over the Eastern Province, with no damage reported. Traders focused instead on the IEA's call for a fourth-quarter surplus as Gulf exports recover, while UBS still sees Brent at $110 by year-end because supply buffers are thin.
stories.why: Unconfirmed incidents no longer move the flat price, but mine risk keeps freight and insurance costs high: the war premium is shifting from crude to shipping.

stories.title: Asian chip stocks crash on the eve of Nvidia results
stories.lead: Taiwan's benchmark fell 6.03% to 41,040, its second-largest point drop on record, with TSMC down 5.7%. The KOSPI lost about 4% and SK Hynix 5.6%.
stories.body: Doubts over Nvidia after Jensen Huang's resignation weigh on the whole chain: Nvidia's market value has fallen from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion. Weak Chinese October activity data and a 0.1% annualised contraction in Japan's third-quarter GDP added pressure. Over the weekend the FT reported Huang is weighing a comeback and the WSJ said Washington plans to name AI firms as national champions; Nvidia reports on Tuesday, with about $109 billion of revenue expected, and Anthropic's Nasdaq listing follows two days later.
stories.why: Chips drive demand narratives for copper, power and gas through data centres; a sharp reset in AI spending expectations would ripple into those markets.

stories.title: Gold falls below $3,900 as Fed hike bets build
stories.lead: Spot gold dropped 0.4% to $3,868.88, a one-year low, after a 4.5% weekly loss; silver fell 2.1% to $47.74.
stories.body: CME FedWatch prices a 94% chance of a 25 basis point Fed hike on December 9 and 6% for 50 points, with the US 10-year yield at 5.14% and the dollar index at 103.44. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks on Monday and the October minutes are due Wednesday. Goldman Sachs cut its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650 from $4,800.
stories.why: Rising real yields are overpowering war-driven safe-haven demand, a reminder that gold trades as a rates asset first.

stories.title: Europe enters winter with gas storage far below normal
stories.lead: Dutch TTF eased 0.9% to EUR 90.11/MWh on Monday after a weekly gain of about 12%. EU storage stands at 70.6% against a five-year seasonal average of 89%, and Germany's at 57%.
stories.body: Last week's rally came from unplanned Norwegian outages at Troll and Asgard, colder forecasts and disrupted Gulf LNG exports, which force Europe to compete with Asia for cargoes. Goldman Sachs sees TTF reaching EUR 150/MWh in the first quarter of 2027.
stories.why: A storage gap of nearly 20 points at the start of the heating season makes European gas the most asymmetric price risk in energy this winter.

stories.title: US diesel drops below $6 a gallon
stories.lead: The US national average for diesel fell to $5.998 a gallon on November 14, a two-month low and 8% below the record $6.519 of September 22. Gasoline is below $4.
stories.body: Brent has dropped 18.5% over two weeks, autumn demand is softening and refinery maintenance is largely over. The IEA's emergency release will make 71 million barrels available by end-February, including 15 million barrels of diesel.
stories.why: Refining margins are normalising, gasoline first: the product cracks that drove the inflation spike are starting to unwind.

stories.title: Oil jumps 3% as Houthis claim strikes on Saudi export lifeline
stories.lead: Brent settled at $95.82 (+3.3%) and WTI at $88.74 (+2.6%) on Thursday after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy sites. On Friday Brent was flat near $95.4, on track for a second weekly loss of about 2.4%.
stories.body: The Houthis said they hit a pumping station on the East-West pipeline, a facility in Yanbu and an Aramco building in Riyadh; the Saudi-led coalition said it downed two drones and no damage was confirmed. Iran's military also said four tankers were struck by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, and Ukrainian drones hit the Russian port of Ust-Luga. Prices held despite a 4.7 million barrel US crude build, against an expected draw of 1.1 million, while President Trump said Washington no longer needs a deal with Iran and will keep its blockade.
stories.why: Yanbu, fed by the East-West pipeline, is Saudi Arabia's main export outlet while Hormuz is disrupted, carrying about 4 million barrels a day. Attacks on that corridor target the one route that offsets the strait.

stories.title: US 10-year near 5.13%, gold bounces off a 13-month low
stories.lead: Treasury yields jumped more than 12 basis points on some maturities on Thursday, led by the short end. Spot gold rebounded 1% to about $3,915 on Friday but is down about 3.5% on the week.
stories.body: Markets fully price a 25 basis point Fed hike in December and some investors consider 50, with bets extending beyond December after hot October inflation. The dollar index held near 103.2 and silver near $50.1. US producer prices for October are due on Friday.
stories.why: Higher yields and a firm dollar weigh on precious metals, while the producer price data will show whether the oil shock is feeding into industrial prices.

stories.title: European gas rally extends as heating season starts
stories.lead: Dutch TTF traded near EUR 96.7/MWh on Friday, up about 4.8% on the day and about 13% on the week.
stories.body: Prompt contracts are driven by winter supply worries as the heating season begins and by Gulf shipping risks, while Russia-Ukraine peace talks weigh only on longer-dated contracts. US Henry Hub slipped to $3.30 and EU carbon permits rose to EUR 90.38.
stories.why: Gas is decoupling from oil: Brent is down on the week while TTF surges, a clear case of a near-term risk premium in the forward curve.

stories.title: Congress eyes tighter China chip curbs; Applied Materials beats
stories.lead: House Speaker Mike Johnson said a consensus is forming in Congress to limit AI chip exports to China, after Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia. Applied Materials reported record quarterly revenue of $10.41 billion, above the $10.30 billion expected.
stories.body: Lawmakers are pushing at least four bills on export oversight, chip tracking, equipment sales and remote data center access, and Huang is expected to testify before November 26. Chinese AI stocks fell, with Z.AI down 12%, and Nvidia closed Thursday down 4.3%. Applied Materials guided to about $11.1 billion next quarter versus $10.89 billion expected; after-hours moves varied by source.
stories.why: Equipment demand for AI chips remains strong, but the main risk is shifting to export policy, which shapes demand for the metals and power behind data centers.

stories.title: Iran's Guards claim strike on US radar in Bahrain
stories.lead: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Friday they targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, the first such claim against US military assets in a Gulf state since early September.
stories.body: The Guards called it retaliation for an air attack on a telecom tower in Iran's Hormozgan province. No damage was confirmed and there was no immediate US or Bahraini comment.
stories.why: The fragile lull is fraying just as the oil market bets on a lasting blockade without renewed large-scale fighting.

stories.title: Iran strikes ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in Hormuz
stories.lead: Three sources confirmed to Reuters an attack claimed on Tuesday by the Revolutionary Guards; smoke was visible but damage was not assessed.
stories.body: Shipping and maritime security sources expect a limited impact on commercial traffic, as other navigation systems exist. Gulf oil exports recovered to more than 80% of pre-war levels in September and October, helped by US military escorts, higher Saudi exports via Yanbu and ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar and Fujairah.
stories.why: Iran is now hitting infrastructure on neutral territory while the market prices peace, a reminder that Hormuz flows depend on workarounds that can be disrupted.

stories.title: Oil drops 1.6% on diplomacy hopes over Iran and Ukraine
stories.lead: Brent fell to $91.29 (-$1.47) and WTI to $85.29 (-1.43%) in Asian trade, after gaining 1.4% on Wednesday.
stories.body: A report pointed to further US-Iran diplomacy, while Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed a major prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi without progress on territory. Higher OPEC+ output in October and a 9 million barrel API crude build added to oversupply worries; EIA data is due on Thursday, delayed by Veterans Day.
stories.why: The risk premium built on Wednesday vanished overnight, showing how fast headlines now swing crude around $90.

stories.title: Nvidia board reportedly prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang
stories.lead: Nvidia fell more than 8% after hours to $159.51, having lost over $450 billion in market value since the probe was announced on November 8.
stories.body: The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was meeting on Wednesday evening to decide on Huang's future after an internal investigation into his conduct; no official decision has been announced. Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.97% and Korea's Kospi fell 1.26%, dragged by Nvidia suppliers Samsung and SK Hynix.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest weight in tech indices and the bellwether of AI chip demand, which drives power and copper demand from data centers; results are due on November 17.

stories.title: Gold slips below $4,000 as a 50 bp Fed hike enters the debate
stories.lead: Spot gold fell 0.4% to $3,973 an ounce and silver 0.6% to $51.36, with the dollar index at 102.98.
stories.body: A 25 bp Fed hike in December is fully priced and some investors now consider 50 bp, after Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called October inflation borderline disturbing. The US 2-year yield jumped 18 bp on Tuesday and the 10-year trades near 5%.
stories.why: Rising real rates weigh on non-yielding metals, and the Fed path now hinges on whether the energy shock spreads to wider prices.

stories.title: First Russian diesel cargo for the US idles off the East Coast
stories.lead: The White House plan allows 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel now, 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes after that; US diesel costs $6.13 a gallon, up 63% since February.
stories.body: Importers hesitate because of legal liability, bank reluctance to finance the deals and the need to blend the fuel to meet NYMEX heating oil specifications, while senators from both parties ask for the waiver to be rescinded. In Europe, northwest gasoline refining margins fell by more than $28 to $8.38 a barrel.
stories.why: Sanctions, financing and product specs can strand a cargo even when policy allows it, which keeps distillate cracks decoupled from crude.

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes knock out about 30% of Russia's refining capacity
stories.lead: Nine of Russia's 35 major refineries were disrupted in a week, about 2.2 mb/d of nameplate capacity out of roughly 6.8 mb/d.
stories.body: Industry estimates put the real loss of crude runs at up to 200,000 tonnes a day, around 1.5 mb/d, after refineries had partly recovered to about 5 mb/d at the end of October. The drone campaign has been running since late October and targets processing rather than crude exports.
stories.why: Less Russian refining means more crude available for export and fewer barrels of diesel, so product cracks and spreads can move independently of Brent.

stories.title: Oil edges back toward $92 as Iran deal hopes fade
stories.lead: Brent trades around $91.9 to $92.1 (+0.4 to 0.6%) and WTI near $86.4 after dipping below $90 on Tuesday.
stories.body: Up to 37 vessels were attacked near Hormuz in October, a record, and the IMO counts 130 since the war began; LSEG notes that higher flows would still depend on mine clearance, insurance and shipowners. On the supply side, OPEC output rose to 22.87 mb/d in October, about 90% of February levels, and the API reported a 9.0 million barrel build in US crude stocks.
stories.why: The paper market prices diplomacy while logistics remain the real bottleneck; official EIA stocks on Thursday and the IEA report on Friday are the next checks.

stories.title: Orlen cancels a long-term Qatar LNG contract; TTF rises 2.7%
stories.lead: Poland's Orlen is the first QatarEnergy customer to cancel a long-term deal, a 1 Mt per year contract signed in 2009 and running to 2034.
stories.body: QatarEnergy has been under force majeure since spring 2026, extended at the end of October to year-end. Qatari LNG exports fell to about 2.7 Mt in October from close to 6.2 Mt in February, even as LNG transits through Hormuz rose to 31. European gas climbed to about EUR87/MWh, with EU storage below 73% against a five-year average of 89%.
stories.why: A prolonged force majeure starts to break long-term contracts, pushing volumes toward the spot market and trader portfolios.

stories.title: Siemens Energy posts a record year but guides 2027 profit below consensus
stories.lead: Fourth-quarter revenue hit a record EUR12.83bn and the backlog EUR164bn, but 2027 net income guidance of about EUR5bn is roughly 10% below the EUR5.5bn consensus.
stories.body: Full-year 2026 net income rose to EUR4.13bn from EUR1.69bn, with a proposed dividend of EUR2.30. Quarterly orders of EUR14.82bn missed the EUR15.47bn expected. Gas turbines and grid equipment for data centers drive growth, with Gas Services revenue seen up 24 to 26% in 2027 and a 20 to 22% margin targeted for 2030.
stories.why: Data center power demand keeps turning into firm orders for gas turbines and grid equipment, a structural support for gas burn and copper-intensive grids.

stories.title: Wall Street slips after hot CPI; futures and Asia rebound on chips
stories.lead: On Tuesday the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Nasdaq 0.74%, with Nvidia down 5.5%; this morning Nasdaq 100 futures are up 1.4% and the Kospi 2.6%.
stories.body: October CPI rose 0.4% month on month, above expectations. Nvidia's market value fell to about $4.07tn, its lowest since late March, amid the Jensen Huang affair. TSMC gained 2.2% after its board approved up to $1bn of investments in Anthropic and OpenAI, and the Nikkei rose 1.31%. The US bond market is closed today for Veterans Day.
stories.why: The chip supply chain, not Nvidia, is leading the rebound ahead of Nvidia's results on 17 November, a key test for AI-driven demand for chips, power and metals.

stories.body: Donald Trump said a new strike on Iran was unnecessary "at this stage", Qatar called for restraint and tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is picking up, to the point that Middle East producers are cutting prices to find buyers. Physical Gulf crude tells a different story: Abu Dhabi's Murban rose 3.4% to $99.17, about $7 above Brent, and attacks on ships near the strait continue.
stories.lead: Brent closed at $92.57 on Monday (-5.85%) and slipped again to about $91.3 to $92.3 this morning; WTI trades near $86 to $87.
stories.title: Oil: Brent at its lowest since 31 August as Hormuz flows resume
stories.why: The gap between paper and physical Gulf crude widened from about $1.70 to about $7 in a day. That spread is where physical traders make or lose money, and the EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook out today gives the official US read.

stories.body: Exports of integrated circuits more than doubled (+137.1%) to $39.59bn on AI-related demand. The cumulative surplus since January passes $1,040bn.
stories.lead: Exports rose 35.2% year on year (about $412bn) and imports 41.6% (about $307bn), both well above forecasts; the surplus narrowed to $105.3bn.
stories.title: China: imports jump 41.6% in October, trade surplus at its lowest since April
stories.why: Imports this strong support commodity demand at a time when physical copper is already tight in China. The product detail (crude, copper) comes with the full customs data.

stories.body: Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee has warned that the data-centre build-out looks like old-fashioned demand overheating. Markets priced about an 81% chance of a Fed hike on 9 December (CME FedWatch, cited by Reuters).
stories.lead: Core is expected at +0.2% after +0.6% headline and +0.3% core in September; no year-on-year rate will be published because October 2025 data are missing after the shutdown.
stories.title: US October CPI due at 14:30 Paris time: +0.3% m/m expected
stories.why: It is the last inflation print before the Fed meeting; a reading above 0.3% would reinforce the curve flattening seen since Friday's jobs report.

stories.body: This morning Korea's Kospi rose 4% to 5%, enough to trigger the brake on programme orders, the Nikkei 2.89% (SoftBank +13.4%, Tokyo Electron +4.7%) and SK Hynix 5.2%; S&P 500 futures are up 0.16%.
stories.lead: The S&P 500 gained 2.35%, the Nasdaq Composite 2.74% and the Dow 1,104 points (+2.2%) on Monday, while Nvidia fell about 4% on its board's inquiry into Jensen Huang.
stories.title: Wall Street posts its best day since 8 April; Asia follows on chipmakers
stories.why: After last week's AI sell-off, the rebound is led by equipment and memory makers rather than Nvidia, eight days before Nvidia's results on 17 November.

stories.body: Janus Henderson launched an active China equity ETF and Defiance the first equal-weight UCITS ETF on the Magnificent Seven. J.P. Morgan AM named Eve-Marie Bussière, from DWS, head of ETF distribution for France and Monaco.
stories.lead: Fidelity International launched an Equity Enhanced Yield range and now has more than thirty active ETFs; Man Group launched two (trend following and infrastructure).
stories.title: Active ETFs in Europe: Fidelity passes thirty products, Man Group launches its first UCITS active ETFs
stories.why: Active ETFs change the market maker's job: less transparent baskets and harder hedging.

note: Veille 2026-11-09, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Brent slips to $96.45 after Trump, but physical Gulf crude rises
stories.lead: Brent fell 1.9% after a weekly drop of more than 16%, the steepest since 2020; WTI trades near $90.5 to $91.3.
stories.body: Donald Trump called a new strike on Iran very unlikely while talks progress. Abu Dhabi's Murban, a physical Gulf grade, rose 3.4% to $99.17, about $1.70 above Brent: a tanker was hit again in the Strait of Hormuz on 8 November and IMF PortWatch counted a single transit on 1 November against 85 a day before the crisis. JPMorgan still sees a global surplus of 1.4 mb/d in October.
stories.why: The gap between a paper market pricing peace and a still tight physical market is exactly what traders arbitrage.

stories.title: Nvidia board opens an inquiry into Jensen Huang, shares about -6% in early trading
stories.lead: Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1% and S&P 500 futures 0.15%.
stories.body: On 8 November Jensen Huang acknowledged a relationship with a woman US agencies describe as a Chinese spy; a committee of independent directors is investigating and says it has no reason to believe secrets leaked. Friday had brought a rebound (Nasdaq +1.09%, S&P 500 +0.31%), and Taiwan's market rose 4.94% on Monday.
stories.why: A governance risk on the largest S&P 500 company, a week before its results on 17 November 2026.

stories.title: Copper: record physical squeeze in China, Trafigura buys at rising premiums
stories.lead: Shanghai's spot premium hit a record 2,615 yuan ($392) a tonne after tripling in two weeks; import premiums rose more than 40% to $195 to $210.
stories.body: The spread between the first two SHFE contracts topped 1,200 yuan, unseen since 2005, and deliverable stocks (33,848 t) cover less than a day of Chinese demand. Smelters lack concentrate and scrap, copper and cobalt trucks were seized in the DR Congo, and metal stayed in the United States on tariff fears. Trafigura has been asking producers and traders for November and December cargoes (Bloomberg).
stories.why: A concrete case of backwardation and physical premium on a key energy transition metal.

stories.title: Credit Agricole proposes to merge its Italian arm with Banco BPM
stories.lead: Friendly offer with a 20% premium for Banco BPM shareholders and a €1 billion special dividend.
stories.body: Credit Agricole would go from 29.6% to about 45% of a new group, Italy's third largest bank, listed in Milan. The deal needs a Banco BPM shareholder vote under the whitewash procedure, plus approval from the ECB and the Italian government; completion is targeted for the second half of 2027. UniCredit rose 4.7% the same morning on a record quarterly profit of €3.3 billion.
stories.why: European bank consolidation continues, with French and Italian lenders at the center.

stories.title: US October CPI due tomorrow: +0.2% to +0.3% month on month expected
stories.lead: FactSet expects +0.24% after +0.6% in September; core is seen near +0.2%.
stories.body: The BLS will not publish a year-on-year rate, for lack of October 2025 data after the shutdown. The probability of a Fed hike on 9 December 2026 is about 81% (CME FedWatch, via Reuters). In China, October producer prices rose 5.7% from a year earlier, the highest since June 2022, while consumer prices slowed to +0.7%.
stories.why: The last inflation print before the Fed, which will shape the flattening of the yield curve.

note: Veille 2026-11-06, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: AI stocks crash: S&P 500 -4.4%, Nasdaq -5.5%, chip index -12.2%
stories.lead: Worst S&P 500 session since April 2025; the Nasdaq Composite is 11.9% below its October record, in correction territory.
stories.body: Nvidia fell 9.3% and AMD 17.3%, while AppLovin jumped 31% on results. Investors fear a freeze on data centers after the Democratic wave, with about forty local measures to slow their construction and a call for a national moratorium, plus doubts on AI returns and higher borrowing costs. Money moved into Treasuries: the 10-year yield fell to 4.84% from 4.90%.
stories.why: A textbook flight to quality: equities down, long rates down, with the AI supply chain at the center.

stories.title: Asia follows: Nikkei about -5.9%, Kospi halted, Taiex -4.5%
stories.lead: The Kospi touched -8.8% intraday and lost about 11.7% over the week; TSMC fell as much as 8.5% in Taipei.
stories.body: SK Hynix lost about 10% and Samsung about 8%; Kioxia, SoftBank and Advantest also dropped sharply. China held up better (Hang Seng -0.7%). Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down about 1% early on, and gold fell 1.1% to $4,044 an ounce.
stories.why: The markets most exposed to memory and chip equipment pay for US political risk.

stories.title: Brent rebounds to $98.29 as tankers burn near Hormuz
stories.lead: Brent +3.9% to $98.29 and WTI to $91.07 after Wednesday's crash.
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers and a tug caught fire after using unauthorised routes in the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO counts at least five incidents in the Gulf since Sunday, and US crude and product stocks are falling. Eurasia Group cut the odds of a deal with Iran to 10% from 20% and sees Brent at $110 to $125 if tensions escalate.
stories.why: The geopolitical premium rebuilds as soon as maritime incidents resume, with freight, insurance and the Brent-WTI spread ($7.22) moving with it.

stories.title: US October jobs report today: about 60,000 to 65,000 jobs expected
stories.lead: Release at 14:30 Paris time, with unemployment seen at 4.2%.
stories.body: September added only 29,000 jobs and the monthly average since January 2025 is about 35,000. Signals this week were firm: ADP at 86,000, jobless claims at their lowest since July and JOLTS at 7.5 million. Markets price a 67% chance of a 25 basis point Fed hike on 9 December 2026 (CME FedWatch).
stories.why: A strong number would back a December hike while equities fall; a weak one would extend the rally in long bonds.

note: Veille 2026-11-05, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Brent crashes 9.73% to $93.52, its biggest drop in months
stories.lead: Brent lost $10.08 on Wednesday to its lowest since 4 September 2026 and held near $93.6 on Thursday morning, against almost $118 on 30 October.
stories.body: The White House tied the Republican defeat in the midterms to the war with Iran, and the market started to price a deal. The physical market stays tight: US distillate stocks are 13% below their five-year average and Gulf exports fell to 17.1 mb/d in October from 18.9 mb/d in September, about three quarters of pre-war levels (Vortexa).
stories.why: Paper markets may have erased the Hormuz premium faster than physical flows justify.

stories.title: Bank of England expected to raise rates for the first time since August 2023
stories.lead: A Reuters poll sees a 7-2 vote to lift Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% at 13:00 Paris time.
stories.body: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, above expectations, on the energy shock from the war with Iran. Markets also price at least three more quarter-point hikes next year, which would take UK rates above US rates; some economists, such as PIMCO, expect only one, in February 2027.
stories.why: The gap between market pricing and economists is a live debate for sterling rates, and the oil slide may soften the Bank's message.

stories.title: Qualcomm beats on revenue but guides below, shares down about 6% after hours
stories.lead: Fourth-quarter revenue of $10.32 billion against $10.12 billion expected; adjusted EPS of $2.17.
stories.body: Handsets fell 26% from a year earlier while automotive and IoT rose 36%. The first-quarter outlook of $2.15 to $2.35 per share sits below the roughly $2.32 expected, because component costs, memory first, are rising; the $5 billion data center revenue goal for 2027 is unchanged.
stories.why: AI demand lifts memory prices and squeezes the margins of mobile chip makers: winners and losers from the same trend.

stories.title: Dow posts its best session since April 2025, Asia split on Thursday
stories.body: The end of election uncertainty and the fall in oil drove the rally. On Thursday the Nikkei fell about 1.5% on AI names, on fears that a Democratic Congress regulates data centers, while the broader Topix rose; gold traded near $4,135 an ounce.
stories.why: A clear rotation: cyclicals and banks up, AI down on political risk.

stories.title: ArcelorMittal posts a net loss on the Kryvyi Rih shutdown, adjusted profit rises
stories.lead: Third-quarter net loss of $391 million after $852 million of impairments and $293 million of exceptional charges tied to the Ukrainian site.
stories.body: Adjusted net income rose to $868 million from $683 million in the second quarter, and EBITDA of about $2.02 billion beat the $1.96 billion consensus (LSEG). Net debt reached $10.3 billion at end-September, swollen by $2.5 billion of working capital expected to unwind in the fourth quarter; the group sees double-digit growth in European flat steel shipments.
stories.why: Europe's steel demand is turning up while the war keeps weighing on Ukrainian iron ore and steel capacity.

note: Veille 2026-11-03, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Oil rebounds about 1% after a reported US strike on Qeshm, a day after a 7.6% slide
stories.lead: Brent closed Monday at $104.77 (-7.63%) and WTI at $96.46 (-7.4%), then climbed back to about $106 and $96.9 on Tuesday morning.
stories.body: Monday's drop followed signs of diplomacy between Washington and Tehran. Overnight, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, a US strike on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz, described as defensive and not confirmed by CENTCOM. JD Vance said he was optimistic about a negotiated settlement, and Donald Trump answered no when asked whether he would strike Iran after the elections.
stories.why: Diplomacy and limited strikes now move together, so the Hormuz risk premium can vanish or return within a single session.

stories.title: Reserve Bank of Australia lifts its cash rate to 4.85%, the highest since 2008
stories.lead: Fifth hike of 2026, from 4.60% to 4.85%, voted six to three.
stories.body: The central bank pointed to high inflation, the war in the Middle East and the rise in oil prices. Governor Michele Bullock left the door open to further hikes but hinted at a pause to assess the effect of the five moves; the three dissenters wanted to hold.
stories.why: A first clear case of a central bank tightening because of the oil shock, ahead of the Bank of England decision on Thursday.

stories.title: Wall Street ends lower despite oil, Apple slips after results
stories.lead: The S&P 500 lost 0.51% to 7,541.40, a third straight fall, and the Nasdaq 1.07%, while the Dow gained 0.41%.
stories.body: After the close, Apple reported quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion (+12%), including $57.6 billion from the iPhone (+17%), but fell about 3% after hours on a lower gross margin outlook tied to memory costs. Palantir, with revenue up 96% and a raised annual outlook, also slipped about 3%.
stories.why: Memory costs are becoming a common thread across the chip and hardware chain, a sign of how AI demand reprices inputs.
